1.heading: Thus saith:
refs: Whether the rules for public worship here laid down were designed to be observed in those things wherein they differed from the law of Moses, in the ministrations of the second temple, is not certain. In the latter history of the Jewish church, the law of Moses only was followed, except in the corruption of following the traditions of the fathers.
The prophet had before observed that the east gate of the outer court was shut, and was told that it must only be opened for the prince
and now he is informed that the gate of the inner court on the east was also shut, and is to be opened only on the sabbath and new moons, till the evening.

4.heading: the burnt:
refs: The proportions of the burnt offerings, and also of the meat and drink offerings, are very different here form those prescribed in the Mosaic law. The meat offering, under the law, was only three tenths of an ephah to a bullock, two tenths for a ram, and one tenth for a lamb, with the fourth part of a hin of oil. Eze 45:17

13.heading: Thou shalt daily:
refs: It is observable, that there is nothing said about the evening sacrifice, or the additional lamb, morning and evening, on the sabbath, which makes an important difference between this and the old laws
and is probably an intimation of that change in the external forms of religion which the coming of the Messiah should introduce. Exod 29:38-42

19.heading: the entry:
refs: This entry was at the west side of the north gate of the inner court. Eze 40:44-46
This place was at the west corners of the inner court, or court of the priests
where they prepared the most holy things, the trespass and sin offering, which none but the priests might eat
that they might not "bear them out into the utter court, to sanctify the people," that is, by touching them incapacitate them from discharging their ordinary occupations.

22.heading: court:
refs: These court in the corners of the outer court, or court of the people, appear to have been a kind of uncovered apartments, surrounded with little chambers for the cooks, and used for dressing the peace offerings of the people. On these their families and friends feasted
and portions were sent to the poor, the widow, and the orphan
and thus the spirit of devotion preserved the spirit of mercy, charity, and benevolence, in the land.
22.body:
